summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations rose 28.7% to INR68.4 crores and PAT to INR38.3 crores, with Q4 PAT turning to INR10.5 crores from a loss.
summary.overview: Wealth First reported FY26 consolidated revenue from operations of INR68.4 crores (up 28.7% from INR53.2 crores) and PAT of INR38.3 crores (vs INR34.1 crores). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR16.5 crores versus a loss of INR3.3 crores in Q4 FY25, helped by insurance sales, ARR asset flows and no MTM drag after the trading book was taken to zero. Management framed FY26 as a transition year: AMC licence received, insurance broking licence obtained, and the equity trading book exited. Cost-to-income rose to 29.9% (ex one-offs) from 23%, which management attributed to strategic and growth investments.

segments.name: Wealth management (core business activity)
segments.commentary: Largest and most stable revenue contributor. Bond AUM INR4,014 crores (up 7.3%), direct equity AUM INR2,272 crores (up 2.2%), fixed deposit AUM INR234 crores (up 10.6%), trail-based AUM INR5,558 crores.

segments.name: Insurance (Wealthshield Insurance Brokers)
segments.commentary: Insurance top line about INR7.5 crores in FY26 after the Q2 licence. Management expects 20-25% growth over the next two to three years and roughly 15-20% of total business revenue by FY28.

segments.name: Lakshya AMC (under set-up)
segments.commentary: SEBI final licence received. INR41 crores invested by Wealth First (the company has also said INR60-61 crores subscribed in total), with minimum net worth of INR50 crores. Around nine professionals onboarded.

segments.name: Trading book
segments.commentary: Equity trading book reduced to zero in FY26. Government and tax-free bond holdings of about INR27 crores remain in the books and are treated as accrual/liquidity holdings.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable cost-to-income ratio targeted at 20-25% once AMC and insurance mature (management said 'less than 30', range 20-30).
Insurance expected to grow 20-25% over the next two to three years.
Insurance revenue to pick up in FY28, reaching roughly 15-20% of total business revenue.
Lakshya AMC to file first products with SEBI around 5-10 June 2026; target of at least three products in the next 12 months.
One inorganic acquisition outside Gujarat targeted, partly deployed in the next three to six months; infrastructure expansion around Q3 FY27.
Dividend policy: minimum 30% of consolidated PAT.
capex_capacity: Lakshya AMC: INR41 crores invested by Wealth First, with no major further capital needed for at least a year per management. Dedicated Ahmedabad office set up.
Wealthshield: six insurance staff hired; expected to reach around 15-20 people in the next year, plus POSPs.
Offices: Ahmedabad (main), Pune (Wakad, about three years old) and Surat (opened about six months ago). One or two presences outside Gujarat planned in coming months.
Capital released from trading book being redeployed to AMC capitalisation, one inorganic deal and infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Net equity inflows into ARR assets were INR386 crores in FY26. AUA growth of 4.6% was entirely net-sales driven because equity markets were negative over the past year.
A 12-14% market correction in Q4 FY26 compressed closing portfolio values and reduced reported year-end AUA.
Client base grew 5% to 21,746 clients (987 individual clients added). Client families rose 5% to 6,889 (311 added).
Client acquisition is mainly word-of-mouth and investor-awareness programmes, with a 50-70% conversion over time, per management.
Index-based PMS for NRI clients in the US and Canada launched early in FY26; early response described as encouraging.

qa_highlights.question: How much has been invested in the AMC and will more capital be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said INR60 crores subscribed, then corrected to INR61 crores; Nishil Pandya confirmed Wealth First's share is INR41 crores. Minimum net worth is INR50 crores and about 20% extra has been capitalised. Little further money is needed for at least a year.

qa_highlights.question: When will the first fund launch and what is the 12-24 month pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: First products to be filed with SEBI around 5-10 June 2026, and approval may take time. Target is at least three products in 12 months, all innovative, with no me-too products.

qa_highlights.question: How will the revenue mix change over three to five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance delivered about INR7.5 crores in FY26 (licence in Q2) and is expected to reach roughly 15-20% of business revenue by FY28. AMC revenue size not yet quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Growth expectations for Wealthshield over two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 20-25% growth, driven by cross-selling health and motor to existing clients and a B2B team.

qa_highlights.question: What are the inventory balances on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR134 crores as of 31 March 2026, including INR41 crores in Lakshya AMC. Bond inventory is about INR27 crores and the rest is cash and money market funds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable cost-to-income ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 30%, in a 20-30% range. Once new businesses mature, management expects about 20-25%, and 20-25% for the wealth business.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the non-controlling interest on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: It is the allocation towards the AMC business, since the AMC is partly owned by other partners.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be deployed now that the trading book is zero, and what about government bonds?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital goes to AMC (INR41 crores already), one inorganic deal in the near future (partly within three to six months), and infrastructure around Q3 FY27. Government bonds stay on the books as a liquidity-focused and accrual business; the bond book is only about INR27 crores, and gains or losses on it are routed through trading activities but expected to be minimal.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility depends on net flows, since FY26 AUA growth came only from net sales while markets fell 12-14% in Q4.
Cost-to-income at 29.9% in FY26 and expected to stay elevated while AMC and insurance are being built.
SEBI approval timing for Lakshya AMC's first products is uncertain, and management flagged possible back-and-forth with the regulator.
Insurance growth targets (20-25%) and the FY28 revenue share depend on the new B2B team scaling.
Inorganic acquisition outside Gujarat is still unnamed and undated beyond the next few months.

Inconsistencies in the transcript: the AMC subscription figure was corrected from INR60 to INR61 crores and from INR40 to INR41 crores; the call date (1 June) differs from the letter date (5 June). Verify in the filed audio.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on strategy and the Q4 turnaround, with heavy emphasis on the 'transformation' narrative. Management was more measured on near-term numbers: it conceded the AUA decline from the Q4 correction and was less specific on AMC revenue and product timelines.
key_quotes: Over the last three decades, we built trust. In FY26, we began building the future.
The AUA growth we have delivered is therefore entirely net sales driven, meaning real new money coming in from clients rather than market appreciation doing the heavy lifting.
Historically, this business added volatility to our earnings profile. Exiting the trading book reflects our strategic intent to sharpen focus on our core recurring business.
